stack: Next.js 16.3 (App Router, Turbopack) · React 19 · TypeScript (strict) · Supabase (Postgres + RLS + Storage + Auth) · Vercel
scope: Whole repository at main (cb1567a) plus another session's uncommitted work in the tree; production reached only for public GETs (login, manifest, robots, well-known files). One production build measured. No Lighthouse, no e2e run, no access to the Supabase or Vercel dashboards.
summary: Orbis is carefully built underneath: row-level security on every table, encrypted connection tokens, a privacy-aware AI router, strict TypeScript and friendly error handling. What stands between it and a product strangers pay for is mostly around it, not in it. Right now anyone can sign up on the live site, there is no privacy policy or account deletion (both app stores require them), Gmail and the broker connections need approvals or commercial terms before strangers can use them, and the app renders its whole home page two or three times on every open. The quickest wins (closing sign-up, security headers, stopping the double renders, code-splitting the tabs) are a day or two; store launch and billing are weeks.

security.note: No criticals. 1 high (public sign-up is open on the live site), 5 medium (no security headers, password change without re-auth, push-endpoint SSRF, no upload rate limits, no account deletion), 9 low.

performance.note: 392 KB gzip first-load JS with every tab bundled; Home renders 2–3 times per open; background actions block taps; nothing cached.

seo.note: Only /login and /forgot-password are public; no robots, sitemap, OG tags, privacy page or landing page.

code_quality.note: Strict TS, 1.4% duplication, all deps used; but pnpm test always fails, lint script is broken, no CI, 626-line app shell.

findings.title: Anyone can create an account on the live site
findings.impact: ORBIS_ALLOWED_EMAILS is not set in Vercel, so the Create account button is live. A stranger can store financial and health data in an app with no privacy policy, no terms, no way to delete their account and no upload rate limits (see the medium findings), and every stranger shares your free AI and data-provider quotas.
findings.fix: Set ORBIS_ALLOWED_EMAILS=<your address> in Vercel → Project → Settings → Environment Variables (Production), then redeploy. Open sign-up again deliberately once privacy, terms, deletion and rate limits exist.
findings.manual_action: Set the env var in the Vercel dashboard today. Also check Supabase → Authentication → Users for accounts you do not recognise.

findings.title: Home renders the whole page twice on every open
findings.impact: The Home effect calls router.refresh() on mount and on every return from background, so each open re-runs the ~34-request server render a second time. On 4G that is a visible re-render and double the database load.
findings.fix: Skip the refresh on first mount (ref flag) and only refresh on visibility after the app was hidden for 60 s or more. Better: refresh only the slices that change instead of router.refresh().

findings.title: Every save renders the full page twice (revalidatePath plus router.refresh)
findings.location: app/finance/actions.ts:23 and 53 other revalidatePath('/') calls; 33 router.refresh() call sites e.g. components/orbis-app.tsx:201
findings.impact: A server action that revalidates already returns a fresh page; the client then asks for another one. Saving a journal entry or confirming a transaction costs about 68 database round-trips and two full payloads before the screen settles.
findings.fix: Keep revalidatePath in the actions and delete the router.refresh() calls that follow them. Longer term, tag per-slice caches ('use cache' + cacheTag) so a journal save does not re-query finance, brokers and health.

findings.title: Background Home requests make the user's own taps wait
findings.impact: Next runs server actions one at a time per client. The portfolio fetch and the AI brief (up to 20 s per model) are queued on every Home mount, so tapping Done on a routine, Sync or Save can sit dead for seconds.
findings.fix: Move these reads to GET route handlers called with fetch, or render them server-side inside <Suspense>. Keep server actions for writes.

findings.title: The AI home brief is generated 2–3 times per open and burns the daily quota
findings.impact: The request fires with weather=null, again when weather arrives and again when the portfolio lands; each misses the saved brief. The 12-a-day limit is gone after about five opens, and the written brief appears late.
findings.fix: Wait until weather has settled (ready, error or needs city) and the portfolio has loaded or timed out before asking; debounce data changes.

findings.title: No code splitting: every tab ships in the first download
findings.impact: '/' ships about 392 KB gzip of JavaScript (1.47 MB raw), including recharts and all six tabs, before Home is usable on a mid-range Android phone.
findings.fix: Wrap FinanceScreen, HealthScreen, InvestDashboard, SocialScreen and ProfileScreen in next/dynamic; dynamic-import the recharts chart and PlanView. Expected first load ~200–230 KB gzip.

findings.title: No privacy policy page
findings.impact: Google Play and the App Store both refuse apps without a public privacy-policy URL; Google's OAuth verification needs one too; India's DPDP Act and GDPR require one for financial and health data.
findings.fix: Add app/privacy/page.tsx (static, indexable): data collected, why, processors (Supabase, Vercel, Google, Zerodha, Groww, the AI providers, weather/market APIs), retention, deletion, grievance contact. Link it from /login and Profile.
findings.manual_action: The legal text needs your approval, ideally a lawyer's review.

findings.title: No account deletion or data export
findings.location: components/personal/profile-screen.tsx:208-211 (Account has Sign out only); no deleteUser anywhere
findings.impact: Blocks both stores (Play account-deletion policy, Apple 5.1.1(v)) and DPDP/GDPR erasure. Deleted journal entries, notes and posts also stay in history tables users cannot clear.
findings.fix: Add deleteAccountAction: require fresh password/passkey, revoke Gmail/Zerodha/Groww, remove the user's folders in every storage bucket, then auth.admin.deleteUser (ON DELETE CASCADE removes rows). Add a public /delete-account page, a 'purge history' option and a JSON/ZIP export.
findings.manual_action: Publish the deletion URL in the Play Console and App Store Connect.

findings.title: Gmail read access needs Google verification and a yearly security assessment
findings.impact: gmail.readonly is a restricted scope. Until Google verifies the app (including a paid, yearly CASA assessment) it stays in testing: 100 users maximum and tokens that expire every 7 days. This blocks selling the automatic expense feature.
findings.fix: Treat Gmail as an opt-in beta. For v1, offer other ways in: statement/CSV import, forwarding alerts to a per-user address, SMS parsing on Android, or India's Account Aggregator network. Drop calendar.readonly if nothing uses it.
findings.manual_action: Start Google OAuth verification (needs a custom domain, a homepage and the privacy policy).

findings.title: Personal data goes to third-party AI without a consent screen
findings.impact: Apple 5.1.2(i) requires telling users and getting permission before personal data is shared with third-party AI; Play's Data safety form must declare it as shared. Undisclosed health-data sharing is a rejection or removal risk.
findings.fix: Add a one-time consent step naming the AI providers and data categories, a switch to turn AI off, and list the providers in the privacy policy.

findings.title: Broker connections are built for one owner
findings.impact: Groww only works for the owner's email; one personal Kite Connect app serving many users likely falls under Zerodha's commercial terms. Selling the app breaks Invest or risks the brokers' terms.
findings.fix: For v1 import holdings from CAS statements (CAMS/KFintech) or CSV. Hide direct broker connections for non-owners until commercial terms are agreed.
findings.manual_action: Ask Zerodha and Groww about multi-user/commercial API terms.

findings.title: A wrapped website risks App Store rejection (guideline 4.2)
findings.location: No ios/, android/ or capacitor config in the repo
findings.impact: A login-gated website in a WebView is a common rejection. Today there is no native value: steps come from a manual Apple Health export upload, and web push does not work inside an iOS WebView.
findings.fix: Wrap with Capacitor (iOS) and a Trusted Web Activity or Capacitor (Android) and add real native features: native push, HealthKit and Health Connect steps, Face ID / fingerprint unlock, the share sheet for Social, home-screen widgets.

findings.title: No Digital Asset Links file for an Android TWA
findings.impact: Without it a Trusted Web Activity shows a browser URL bar and looks like a web wrapper to Play reviewers.
findings.fix: After generating the Android app, add public/.well-known/assetlinks.json with the package name and the Play App Signing SHA-256 (add get_login_creds so passkeys work in the app).
findings.manual_action: Copy the SHA-256 from Play Console → App integrity.

findings.title: pnpm test always fails
findings.location: vitest.config.ts; 13 of 18 lib/**/*.test.ts files use node:test
findings.impact: vitest reports 'No test suite found' for node:test files and exits 1; node's own runner can't resolve '@/' imports in three of them. No single command runs all 143 test cases green, so nothing can gate a release.
findings.fix: Convert the 13 files to vitest (swap the import to vitest; keep node assert or use expect) and add coverage.

findings.title: No linter or formatter, and the lint script is broken
findings.impact: next lint was removed in Next 16, so the script fails; nothing checks React hook rules or style.
findings.fix: npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . ; add eslint.config.mjs (next/core-web-vitals, react-hooks) and Prettier or Biome.

findings.title: No continuous integration
findings.impact: Nothing checks types, tests or the build on push; a buyer's due diligence flags this immediately.
findings.fix: GitHub Actions: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, tsc --noEmit, lint, vitest run --coverage, next build, pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high.

findings.title: No security headers (CSP, frame blocking, HSTS, nosniff, referrer, permissions)
findings.impact: The screen with the PIN pad and broker-key form can be framed by any site (clickjacking), and there is no second line of defence if an XSS ever lands. X-Powered-By: Next.js is sent.
findings.fix: poweredByHeader: false, plus headers() for Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none', Supabase hosts in connect/img/media-src, a nonce for the inline theme script), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy (camera=(), microphone=(self), geolocation=(self)).

findings.title: Password can be changed without re-authentication, even while the app is locked
findings.impact: Anyone with a signed-in browser (a locked phone left open, or a stolen session cookie) can set a new password and take over the account. The PIN/passkey lock guards the app's server actions but not the data API.
findings.fix: Allow updatePassword only with a fresh recovery/OTP sign-in, or with the current password plus an unlocked app. Describe the lock honestly in the UI or move it into RLS with a short-lived 'unlocked' claim.
findings.manual_action: Supabase → Auth: enable 'Secure password change' and 'Leaked password protection'.

findings.title: Push endpoints can point anywhere (blind SSRF and fan-out from the cron)
findings.impact: RLS lets users insert push_subscriptions directly, bypassing the https check and 10-device cap. The dispatcher then POSTs to every stored URL every 5 minutes with no timeout, so one account can make Orbis hit arbitrary hosts and delay everyone's notifications. notification_log rows can also be edited to dodge the test-send limit.
findings.fix: Add a CHECK limiting endpoint hosts to the real push services, revoke direct INSERT/UPDATE (write through the server action only), pass { timeout: 5000 } to web-push and limit concurrency; revoke update on notification_log and grant update (read_at) only.

findings.title: No rate limits or storage quotas on uploads, parsing and sync
findings.location: next.config.ts:7 (bodySizeLimit 101mb); app/health/library-actions.ts:57-84; app/health/actions.ts:131-144; storage policies for social-media and journal-voice
findings.impact: Any account can loop 100 MB document parses, embedding calls, Gmail syncs, or direct uploads to the media buckets with no per-user quota: cost and storage exhaustion. (AI features themselves have daily caps.)
findings.fix: Add a per-user token bucket (Postgres RPC like the existing consume_* functions, or Upstash) on uploads, parse and sync; cap documents and total bytes per user; issue signed upload URLs instead of open bucket INSERT.

findings.title: Large uploads cannot work on Vercel (server-action body limit)
findings.impact: Vercel functions accept about 4.5 MB per request, so the advertised 100 MB workbook and 50 MB document uploads through server actions fail in production.
findings.fix: Upload straight to Supabase Storage with signed upload URLs (as the social planner does) and process from storage.

findings.title: 34 uncached database calls on every render, served from the wrong region
findings.impact: getPinStatus runs alone before the main Promise.all; finance goes three levels deep; gmail/groww/zerodha connections are each read 2–3 times. Functions default to Washington (iad1) while users and data are in India, so TTFB is estimated at 1–2 s.
findings.fix: Pin functions to the Supabase region (export const preferredRegion or vercel.json regions, e.g. bom1), fold getPinStatus into the Promise.all, share one connections loader, and consider one home_bootstrap RPC.

findings.title: Every render sends every tab's data to the phone
findings.impact: Up to 60 journal bodies, 20 full health-plan documents, 200 social posts with fresh signed URLs and more ride along with Home, and again on every refresh.
findings.fix: Give each tab its own route and loader (/finance, /health, …) or stream them behind Suspense; select plan summaries instead of full plan JSON.

findings.title: Nothing is cached: broker holdings are fetched live on every Home visit
findings.impact: Each return to Home calls Groww/Zerodha again and re-asks for the brief; the installed app has no offline shell.
findings.fix: 'use cache' + cacheTag per user slice with tag invalidation in actions; a 60–120 s cache for holdings; app-shell caching in the service worker.

findings.title: AI requests have no overall deadline
findings.impact: Up to four models are tried in turn, each with its own 20–55 s timeout, so the worst case exceeds the 60 s function limit and the user waits the whole time. Telemetry writes are awaited before the answer returns.
findings.fix: Give the request a total budget shared across attempts, and log with after() from next/server.

findings.title: Wasted Zerodha query on every render
findings.impact: The Promise.all runs five queries but uses four.
findings.fix: Remove it, or share connection rows with getAppConnections.

findings.title: No terms of service or support page
findings.impact: App Store Connect needs a Support URL, Play needs a contact, and selling needs terms that limit liability for AI money and health output.
findings.fix: Add /terms and /support with not-financial/medical-advice language and a contact address.

findings.title: No public landing page; the root redirects to /login
findings.impact: Nothing to rank, nothing to use as the store marketing URL, the Google OAuth homepage or the page a buyer sees.
findings.fix: Add a marketing route group for signed-out visitors: what it does, screenshots, pricing, privacy/terms/support links.

findings.title: Service worker has no offline fallback and registers only when notifications are on
findings.impact: Offline, the installed app shows the browser's error page; this lowers the PWA/TWA quality bar.
findings.fix: Register on every load; add a fetch handler with a cached /offline page and app-shell caching; keep the push handlers.

findings.title: Passkeys will not work inside a native wrapper without associated domains
findings.impact: Passkey sign-in fails in a Capacitor iOS app without webcredentials associated domains.
findings.fix: Serve apple-app-site-association (webcredentials + applinks) and add the Associated Domains entitlement.

findings.title: No billing path that meets store rules
findings.location: package.json (no billing SDK); per-feature caps hard-coded e.g. app/ask/actions.ts:10
findings.impact: Digital subscriptions sold inside the store apps must use Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; there are no plans or entitlements to gate on.
findings.fix: Add plans/entitlements tables and read caps from them; Razorpay or Stripe on the web, RevenueCat (or native IAP/Play Billing) in the apps.

findings.title: Health features need store declarations and disclaimers
findings.impact: Play's Health apps declaration and Data safety entries apply; Apple 1.4.1 covers health advice; HealthKit forbids ads and data resale.
findings.fix: Medical disclaimers on every AI health output, declare health and fitness data, follow HealthKit/Health Connect permission rules when added.

findings.title: Third-party logos and trademarks in the UI
findings.impact: Store IP review risk; Apple restricts use of its marks (5.2.5).
findings.fix: Use text names or brand-approved badges; say 'the Health app'; delete the unused zerodha.svg.

findings.title: The sign-in and app-lock check is hand-copied into about 17 places
findings.location: authed() in app/ask, home, personal/voice, routines, social actions; authenticatedClient() in health/steps, invest, personal, journal, notification actions; lib/gmail/oauth.ts:27
findings.impact: This is the security gate. One copy that drifts (for example, forgets isAppUnlocked) becomes a data leak while the app is locked.
findings.fix: lib/auth/session.ts exporting requireUser(): { supabase, userId, claims } | null, and replace every copy.

findings.title: India time zone, INR and the owner's own details are hard-coded
findings.location: 'Asia/Kolkata' in 34 files with 7+ 'today' helpers; lib/personal/fitness-persona.ts:13 (the owner's 92 kg plan); components/orbis-app.tsx:146 (avatar falls back to 'G'); lib/notifications/push.ts:20
findings.impact: The app is wrong for anyone outside India, and new users see the owner's personal content. Changing it means editing 34 files.
findings.fix: lib/time/zone.ts (dateKey, zonedParts, partOfDay with a tz argument), per-user timezone/currency/locale in the profile with IST/INR defaults; remove owner-specific content.

findings.title: Setup errors meant for the developer are shown to users; no onboarding
findings.impact: Users read 'Apply the Zerodha connections migration in Supabase' or 'Set ZERODHA_API_KEY'. Sign-up goes straight to a mandatory PIN with no welcome or guided first connection.
findings.fix: Show a friendly 'unavailable right now' and log the detail server-side; add a 3–4 step onboarding (name and time zone, choose modules, connect one source or try sample data, set up the lock).

findings.title: No error monitoring and no error or loading boundaries
findings.location: app/ (no error.tsx, global-error.tsx or loading.tsx); no Sentry or analytics
findings.impact: When something breaks for a user you will not know, and they see a blank or broken screen.
findings.fix: Add Sentry (or similar), app/error.tsx, app/global-error.tsx and loading skeletons; privacy-safe product analytics (PostHog EU or self-hosted).

findings.title: The whole app is one client component with tabs in state
findings.impact: Every change touches one file; no tab has its own URL, loading state, error boundary or bundle; the back gesture and deep links are fragile.
findings.fix: Route segments app/(app)/{home,finance,health,invest,social,profile}/page.tsx with a shared nav layout; each loads its own data.

findings.title: Five money formatters with four different rounding rules
findings.impact: The same amount can read differently on Home, Expense, Invest and in notifications.
findings.fix: lib/format/money.ts formatMoney(amount, currency, { compact, decimals }) used everywhere.

findings.title: The riskiest code has no tests
findings.location: lib/finance (sync.ts, parse-alert.ts), lib/workbook/parse.ts, lib/ai/router.ts, lib/crypto, lib/gmail, lib/invest
findings.impact: The bank-alert parser, upload hardening and privacy routing are what a buyer expects to see tested; 12 of 24 lib modules have none.
findings.fix: Fixture-based vitest cases for parse-alert, workbook limits, router sensitivity gating and token encryption; coverage in CI.

findings.title: 'Always include' toggle for health documents silently does nothing
findings.impact: It updates health_documents with the user's client, but that table has no UPDATE policy, so nothing changes and the user is told it worked.
findings.fix: Do the update with the admin client scoped by user_id (like the other health-document writes), or add an owner UPDATE policy for that column.

findings.title: README is out of date
findings.impact: It describes removed features (goals, habits), 12 migrations instead of 30, says advice is not saved (it is), and misses 19 environment variables. A buyer or new developer is misled from the first page.
findings.fix: Rewrite: features, architecture sketch, setup from .env.example, migrations, tests, deploy.

findings.title: Zerodha connect has no state/CSRF check
findings.impact: A crafted callback link can attach the attacker's Kite session to a victim's Orbis, feeding them false holdings.
findings.fix: Copy the Gmail pattern: HMAC-signed state cookie, passed as redirect_params and verified in the callback.

findings.title: Owner's Groww keys granted by email match
findings.impact: In a multi-user product the owner's brokerage is one email match away.
findings.fix: Remove the env-credential fallback, or bind it to a fixed user id.

findings.title: Sign-in reveals whether an account exists; weak password rules
findings.impact: Different messages for unconfirmed vs wrong password; 8-character minimum and no breach check on accounts that hold Gmail and broker access.
findings.fix: One generic message; 10+ characters; Supabase leaked-password protection; passkeys or TOTP as a second factor.

findings.title: Table grants rely on Supabase defaults
findings.impact: Narrow grants are ineffective because authenticated keeps all privileges; RLS is the only gate.
findings.fix: revoke all from public, anon, authenticated, then grant exactly what is intended.

findings.title: One SECURITY DEFINER function has a mutable search_path
findings.impact: Hygiene only (service-role only, schema-qualified body).
findings.fix: alter function public.consume_app_pin_attempt(uuid) set search_path = '';

findings.title: AI router trusts the database for which secret to send and where
findings.impact: Anyone able to edit ai_providers could send SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY or the encryption key to their own host.
findings.fix: Allowlist env var names and base-URL hosts in code.

findings.title: E2E tests use the production service key and create users in production
findings.impact: The most powerful key lives on test machines; test accounts land in the live database.
findings.fix: Separate Supabase project or branch for tests.

findings.title: Raw error messages returned to the browser
findings.impact: Unexpected library errors are shown verbatim.
findings.fix: Typed user-facing errors (like SocialError); generic text for everything else; log the original.

findings.title: Unpinned core dependencies and a moderate uuid advisory
findings.impact: A fresh install can pull a new major unreviewed.
findings.fix: Pin versions, --frozen-lockfile in CI, Dependabot/Renovate, pnpm audit and gitleaks in CI.

findings.title: Home content jumps as the brief, weather and portfolio arrive
findings.impact: Estimated CLS 0.1–0.2; feels unpolished.
findings.fix: Reserve heights and cross-fade the brief text in place.

findings.title: 132 KB global stylesheet on every page
findings.impact: 22 KB gzip render-blocking CSS even on /login.
findings.fix: Move tab CSS into CSS Modules or imports inside the dynamically loaded tabs.

findings.title: Blurred background blobs and a hidden preloaded logo on phones
findings.impact: GPU paint cost on low-end Android and a wasted high-priority request.
findings.fix: .ambient { display: none } in the phone media query; drop priority on the hidden logo.

findings.title: Social images use raw at full resolution
findings.impact: Heavy downloads and layout shift in the Social tab.
findings.fix: next/image with a Supabase remotePattern, or Supabase image transforms plus width/height.

findings.title: No robots.txt or sitemap
findings.impact: Auth pages can be indexed; crawlers get no guidance.
findings.fix: app/robots.ts (disallow /api, /auth) and app/sitemap.ts for the public pages.

findings.title: Short titles, one shared description, no canonical
findings.impact: Weak snippets; duplicate descriptions.
findings.fix: metadataBase + canonical; noindex on /login and /forgot-password; 120–160 character descriptions on public pages.

findings.title: No Open Graph, Twitter card or structured data
findings.impact: Shared links have no preview.
findings.fix: openGraph/twitter metadata, opengraph-image.png, SoftwareApplication JSON-LD on the landing page.

findings.title: Manifest lacks screenshots, categories and shortcuts; colours disagree
findings.impact: Plain install prompt; status bar and splash colours differ from the app.
findings.fix: Add screenshots (narrow/wide), categories, shortcuts; align theme/background colours with light and dark.

findings.title: Dead files and exports
findings.location: lib/ai/openrouter.ts; lib/providers/crypto.ts; LockButton/useLockApp in components/security/app-lock-guard.tsx; 26 unused exports (knip)
findings.impact: Noise, and COINGECKO_API_KEY in .env.example for nothing.
findings.fix: Delete them; add knip to CI.

findings.title: Unused tables still in the schema
findings.impact: Dead schema confuses anyone reading the data model.
findings.fix: A migration that drops them after export, or mark them deprecated.

findings.title: isMissingTable and validId redefined in many files (validId inconsistently)
findings.location: 12 copies of isMissingTable; validId in 4 action files, loose vs strict regex
findings.impact: Drift; the loose regex accepts 36 dashes.
findings.fix: lib/supabase/errors.ts and lib/validate/id.ts (strict UUID).

findings.title: The workbook AI quota is shared by unrelated features
findings.location: consume_workbook_ai_request called from app/health/actions.ts, library-actions.ts and app/home/brief-actions.ts
findings.impact: Home briefs use up the workbook allowance; limits are hard to reason about.
findings.fix: One consume_ai_request(feature, limit) keyed by feature.

findings.title: Dark theme tokens written twice; very long lines
findings.impact: Edits must be made twice; hard to review.
findings.fix: light-dark() tokens; a formatter with printWidth 120.
